unreleased: Retired the Windows desktop app, the CLI and their build; the core's own tests now run on Linux with every build. Fixed on Linux: MBH CSV files with Windows line endings imported nothing, and euro amounts lost their € sign. Persely's Settings shows What's new

Enable Banking groundwork: bank API transactions become import rows (Gránit's day-early dates corrected, cut type names and squeezed spaces matched to existing keywords), and the daemon can make signed bank API calls

Persely fetches transactions straight from the bank: connect, renew or disconnect a bank in Settings, then Import → Fetch from the bank opens an import per account; the overview warns before a connection runs out

changes: Show what changed after an update, and on demand via Help → What's New
Fix What's New dialog: OK button clipped off-screen, and UTF-8 text (e.g. accented characters) rendered garbled
Add self-contained HTML reports (table + interactive charts) generated from favorite queries, via Reports → Favorite Reports
Fix charts: route each topic to income or expense by its net sum instead of showing it on both, and let a favorite report restrict which side(s) render via chart_sides
Fold long tails into an "Others" slice/series in report charts, and sort report tables/charts ascending by amount (Others always last)
Publish resources\ files (e.g. the HTML reports' Chart.js) with releases and sync them onto already-installed clients during self-update

Render HTML report tables as interactive Grid.js grids (sortable, searchable, paginated) instead of plain tables, with tighter row spacing and fixes for a permanent stray scrollbar and mangled chart-title text

Add Database → Prune Last Transactions..., a manual repair tool to remove an account's last N transactions with a preview and confirmation, for when a bad import/edit leaves the tail out of date order and breaks import's insertion-point search
Add logging around import file-format detection and stored-data alignment (PrepareImport), so a failed/empty import is now traceable in the log instead of silent

Fix MBH Bank CSV import broken by a source-encoding bug (missing UTF-8 BOM corrupted the header-sentinel literal) and by an unstripped UTF-8 BOM on the bank's own export files; also handle multi-line quoted CSV fields and preserve genuinely-empty trailing fields when splitting semicolon-separated values
CSV parsing fixes
Add debug logging of each imported row's raw CSV/XML fields alongside its parsed date/type/amount/client/memo
Support MBH Bank's expanded CSV export column layout (7 additional columns before Kiegeszitoinformacio)
Manual category resolve now offers the client's own previously-used categories as selection choices, with the most-used one pre-selected

Add BankAccountCli, a headless console tool that generates favorite reports read-only for scheduled/automated use, now also built and published to the release folder by PackageRelease.ps1 (outside the client update manifest)

Auto-recall a transaction's prior categorization when re-import or manual pruning removes it and a later import brings back the same date/amount/client, instead of asking again; fix a crash in PrepareImport when re-importing pops an account's entire transaction history
Add Store Query.../Store Report... in-app editors to save the current filter or an existing favorite query as a favorite without hand-editing JSON
Add per-side relative dates (right-click a from/to calendar for "Today"/"Start of This Month"/etc.) and keep Periods-menu shortcuts self-updating in saved favorites instead of freezing today's range
Word-wrap long lines in the What's New dialog instead of requiring horizontal scrolling

Fix periodic charts: a period that bucked a topic's overall trend (e.g. a refund month in an otherwise expense-heavy category) was plotted as a positive magnitude on that topic's chart instead of offsetting the total
Add a top-level Makefile building a read-only BankAccountCore subset on Linux (g++/wxBase), the first story of the Linux query daemon

Add a Linux daemon HTTP server skeleton (cpp-httplib) with a hot-reloading read-only db snapshot and a /health route, the second story of the Linux query daemon; fix a cross-platform log-path bug and a stale-pointer bug in Currency's exchange-rate history found along the way

Add a POST /query ad-hoc query endpoint to the Linux daemon (JSON in, JSON tables/charts out), the third story of the Linux query daemon; fix a null-pointer crash on any relative-date query, caused by the daemon never calling SetRealToday() at startup

Add favorite query/report listing and run-by-name endpoints to the Linux daemon, the fourth story of the Linux query daemon; fix favorite_queries.json/favorite_reports.json never being found on Linux due to a hardcoded backslash path

Add an interactive query builder web page to the Linux daemon (form filters, favorite query/report picker, live Grid.js tables and Chart.js charts), the fifth story of the Linux query daemon; fix the same hardcoded-backslash bug for the vendored Chart.js/Grid.js resource paths
Require a shared --token on every route of the Linux daemon (header or query param, constant-time compared), the sixth story of the Linux query daemon
Add a systemd unit and deployment guide for the Linux daemon (env-file-based secrets, dedicated unprivileged user, sandboxing), the seventh story of the Linux query daemon
Add GoogleTest coverage for the Linux daemon's JSON query/favorites API, the eighth and final story of the Linux query daemon

Vendor a trimmed, portable ZipLib (Store+Deflate only) directly into the repo instead of a Windows-only sibling checkout, and let the Linux daemon open a compressed/password-protected BData.baf directly instead of requiring a plain-text export

Revise income/expense chart routing so account/type split their income and expense legs independently while category/client stay net-sign, and a plain currency-sum query renders as one unsided Summary chart; consolidate the Linux daemon's query builder to one chart per currency with a dataset dropdown (Income/Expense/Summary) alongside the chart-kind picker

Serve the Linux daemon's query builder CSS/JS from hot-reloadable daemon/static/ files instead of baking them into the page string, so a styling/behavior edit shows up on the next page load with no daemon rebuild/restart

Fix the Linux daemon's account filter matching nothing unless every account was selected (AccountManager never resolved accounts by name), and fix report/daemon charts sometimes folding a single real category into a pointless one-item "Others" slice or showing an empty "Others" for a category with no actual activity

Fix the Linux daemon's ad-hoc query JSON fields (client/category/type/account filters, favorite query definitions) being decoded via the locale-dependent narrow-string constructor instead of UTF-8, breaking any accented-character filter (e.g. searching "Autó" never matched "Autófókusz")
Show the running APP_VERSION next to the title on the Linux daemon's web query page

Fix the real cause of the Linux daemon's accented-character search bug still failing after the earlier UTF-8 JSON-decode fix: ManagerType's SearchIds/Create/Rename and AccountManager::RenameId checked for an empty name via strlen() on a wxString, forcing it through a locale-dependent narrow-char conversion that silently fails on non-ASCII text under the daemon's uninitialized "C" locale, so any client/category/type/account filter containing an accented character (not just a mismatched one) matched nothing; also stop QueryByName::AddName from forcing every filter name through that same lossy conversion by taking a String directly instead of a const char*

Fix the Linux daemon aborting while loading a BData.baf read over a real Samba/CIFS mount: the vendored ZipLib's sub_streambuf treated a short read (normal on CIFS) as EOF, truncating decompression mid-file; also document copying the daemon's static frontend assets into the systemd WorkingDirectory

Fix the Linux daemon's Type aggregation rendering blank topic labels (table rows and chart legends): TransactionType's constructor took a const char*, so every accented type name loaded from the db went through a locale-dependent narrow-char conversion and came out empty under the daemon's "C" locale

Charts never mix Income and Expense: every chart (desktop, HTML reports, Linux daemon) shows exactly one dataset - Net (new, default), Income or Expense - Net as bar/line only and drawn either side of a zero line; single-entry charts keep fixed colours (Income green, Expense red, Net purple), multi-topic charts are colourful, line charts shade only between the line and zero, and the daemon gains a Currency dropdown with 'Convert all to this currency'
Chart "Convert all to this currency" now converts each transaction at its own date's exchange rate, matching the table's exchanged total
Persely becomes the only app: its own SQLite database on the server, editing and bank-file import in the browser (any device), daily snapshots; the Windows desktop app and CLI are retired
Fix crash when storing a favorite query/report with accented names (JSON now written/read as UTF-8; a failed save no longer empties the file)
HTML report files are now opened via a wide (Unicode) path and a failed write is reported instead of claiming success
Linux web service: new React web app (overview, query explorer, transactions, reports) with Tailscale-login and LAN-password sign-in, shipped as a Docker image
Linux web service: --hash-password hides the password and asks for it twice
Linux web service: deploy/set-secrets.sh writes the secrets file; the daemon refuses the template's placeholder values
Linux web service: the web app is now called Persely, at persely.tail61796b.ts.net

Persely: click any chart or table number for its transactions; transaction search; comparisons, category trends and a stale-data notice on the overview; client pages; year in review; save and delete favorites (the web app's own, kept on the server)
Persely: transaction lists fit a phone's width - long names end in an ellipsis, and the date moves under the name
Persely: 4-digit amounts are grouped too (3 380 Ft, not 3380 Ft)
Persely: clicking a category opens its own page - month-by-month and yearly charts, who was paid, latest transactions - over the clicked period

Persely: a Settings tab, shared by every device - categories left out of the totals, and categories whose money in isn't income (shown as small grey 'other money in'; net and savings rate follow); kept by id, so renaming a category doesn't break them

Persely: find a client or category by name and jump to its page; client and category pages break down by account (or name the only one) and list their 5 largest transactions; transaction lists drop columns every row agrees on and link every name - a client or category to its page, an account to its transactions
Persely: client and category charts switch between bars, lines and net, with an optional trend line and a one-line reading of it
Persely: client and category breakdowns show money out and money in apart (paid to / paid by, spent / received) when it went both ways
Persely: a client, category or account every listed transaction shares is named once above the list, as a link; a single transaction keeps all its columns
Linux daemon: a result in a single foreign currency also carries its HUF conversion, so Persely's totals no longer count euros as forints

Persely: runs from its own SQLite database on the server, converted from BData.baf and verified identical (bankaccount-migrate, refreshed with deploy/migrate-db.sh); the server build is optimized, so queries answer 4-8x faster

Persely: the server can now save changes straight into its database (one transaction per change, recorded with who made it, Tailscale sign-ins only) and keeps daily snapshots on the storage disk; nothing in the web app edits yet

Persely: editing - a transaction's category, client and note, keywords, renaming and merging clients/categories, categorizing by keywords, and MNB exchange rates downloaded on the server; switched off until the cutover (BANKACCOUNT_EDITS=on)

Exchange rates: a weekend or bank holiday is converted with the last rate published before it (Friday's for a Saturday) - only rates on transaction dates used to be kept, so such a day could get a rate up to 6 days old

Persely: import engine - a bank file becomes a step-by-step session (categorize one answer at a time, stop here, review, save), stored in the database and continued from any device; off until the cutover

Persely import: every row is tried with the keywords at once and only the ones that need an answer are asked; after any change (an answer, a keyword, a merge) the rest are worked out again, and nothing reaches the transactions before Save

Persely import screens: upload a bank file (see what's in it first), answer only the rows the keywords can't sort - on a phone, in any number of sittings - review and fix rows, then Save; open imports show on the Overview; off until the cutover
Cutover: Persely is now where bank files are imported and transactions edited; the desktop app's database is no longer read
